phase_task.goal: Sandboxed verification — the single most important requirement. Define the sandbox CONTRACT and build the Python reference runner: apply a patch to a workspace snapshot, build/type-check, run the repo's own tests, all inside an isolated Docker container with network egress denied and CPU/memory/disk/wall-clock limits enforced. "Verified" means the change applied, built, and tests passed IN THE SANDBOX — never on the host, never a model self-report. NO agent loop, NO model calls yet (Phase 4).

deliverables.d: Sandbox contract: implement SandboxClient (replace the Phase-0 stub) with a verify(...) that takes a workspace snapshot + a patch and returns a structured VerificationResult: applied (bool), built (bool), tests_passed (bool), the REAL captured stdout/stderr/exit codes, and resource usage (wall seconds, and whatever cpu/mem the runtime exposes). The result is the oracle — downstream code trusts this, not any model claim. Define it as a stable contract so Phase 8's Go/Rust/TS runners can conform to the same shape.
Python reference runner: executes the apply->build->test pipeline inside a Docker container built from the workspace. All executed code (repo's own + any agent-written patch) is treated as UNTRUSTED.

Isolation, enforced and TESTED (not just configured): network egress default-deny (--network=none or equivalent) so a build/test step cannot phone home or exfiltrate; CPU limit; memory limit; disk/tmpfs quota; wall-clock deadline with hard kill. Non-root, dropped capabilities, read-only rootfs where feasible. State exactly which limits are enforced by what mechanism.

Failure surfacing: a failing build or failing test returns built=false / tests_passed=false with the REAL error output captured and returned (this is what Phase 5 self-repair will read). A passing change returns tests_passed=true with exit 0. No fabricated success anywhere.

Deadline + resource breach handling: a step that exceeds wall-clock is killed and reported as a timeout (not a hang, not a false pass); a step that tries network egress fails closed. Both are explicit result states, not exceptions that crash the caller.
Wire into agentctl for operator inspection (e.g. agentctl sandbox verify --workspace ... --patch ...) showing the structured result + resource usage. Internal/operator only, not a consumer API.

A minimal, deterministic verification fixture on the sample repo: a known-good patch that builds+passes, a known-bad patch that fails tests (with real error text), so the oracle is reproducible without a model.

phase_task.oracle:
Via make test (integration; requires Docker) AND documented manual commands: (1) a known-good patch applied to the sample repo builds and passes tests in the sandbox -> applied=true, built=true, tests_passed=true, exit 0; (2) a known-bad patch -> tests_passed=false with the REAL failure output captured and returned (assert the actual error text is present, not a generic flag); (3) a patch/test that attempts a network call FAILS CLOSED -> egress denied, reported as such, never a pass; (4) a test that runs forever is KILLED at the wall-clock deadline and reported as timeout -> the caller is not hung and does not get a false pass; (5) execution happens in the container, never on the host -> assert the host workspace/filesystem is unmodified by a sandbox run (isolation), and that the runner uses the isolated snapshot; (6) resource limits (cpu/mem/disk) are applied -> demonstrate at least one limit taking effect (e.g. an OOM or cpu-bound case bounded). Each clause must be evidenced by the actual mechanism, no proxies.
DESIGN.md: write the sandbox & egress section — what "verified" precisely means, the apply->build->test pipeline, the exact isolation mechanisms (network, cpu, mem, disk, wall-clock, user/caps/rootfs) and which enforces which, and why untrusted-code execution is safe. Write ADR-0003 (sandbox technology): Docker baseline chosen for the deliverable; the sandbox-as-contract framing (one contract, Phase-8 conforming runners); gVisor/Firecracker named as the production hardening path and why deferred; alternatives considered and rejected. Note the "verification is real" guarantee as the linchpin of the whole platform.
Do not start Phase 4 (agent loop). Report: the SandboxClient/VerificationResult contract as implemented; exactly which resource limits are enforced by which mechanism (network, cpu, mem, disk, wall-clock, user/caps/rootfs); how the real failure output is captured and returned; how the wall-clock kill and egress-deny are proven in tests; and how host isolation is asserted. Flag any limit that is configured-but-not-yet-test-proven so it is not mistaken for verified.
